statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail is low at 10% while Stress is extreme at 81%.
recommendation: Tail remains far below the 25% block threshold, so the deterministic mapping resolves to EA_ON. A DOJ antitrust report on Nvidia's Groq licensing deal was published shortly before this hour and has nudged NQ futures to the lower end of a narrow overnight band, but the reaction is contained: NVDA is down 0.45% after hours and the whole overnight range spans about 0.31%. The extreme Stress reading continues to describe the regime rather than the observed path, with long-end Treasury yields near 52-week highs and Brent above $101 on the unresolved Strait of Hormuz disruption. August PPI prints at 12:30 UTC. A narrow elevated-risk window is flagged from 12:25 to 14:15 UTC around that release and the US cash open; outside it, conditions are described as orderly.
headline: NQ futures slip 0.16% to the low end of a 0.31% overnight band after a DOJ antitrust report on Nvidia's Groq deal, with Brent above $101 and long-end yields near 52-week highs
body:
The Nasdaq-100 closed the 9 September session at 29,421.55, down 0.29%, inside a 29,334.40-29,563.60 range of about 0.78%. In the current overnight hour, NQ futures trade at 29,401.00, down 0.16%, in a 29,389.50-29,480.25 band of roughly 0.31%, sitting near the lower edge after drifting about 64 points over the past hour. The proximate cause is a New York Times report, carried by Reuters, that the Justice Department is examining whether Nvidia's $20 billion Groq licensing deal was structured to avoid antitrust premerger review. NVDA trades at $222.67 after hours, down 0.45%, which is a contained repricing rather than a dislocation, and the total overnight range remains small in absolute terms. That combination keeps Tail low at 10%, a single point above the prior hour to acknowledge a genuine directional tilt and a fresh unpriced technology-regulatory headline landing in thin Asian liquidity.

The stress channels are unchanged and sit outside the index path. Treasury par yields rose again on 9 September to 4.17% at 2 years, 4.83% at 10 years and 5.28% at 30 years, with the 10-year benchmark having tagged a 4.857% intraday 52-week high before settling at 4.837%. Crude is firmer, with WTI at $96.74, up 0.72%, and Brent at $101.57, up 0.36%, holding at the highest levels since May while the Strait of Hormuz remains closed to most traffic and transit counts stay far below the pre-crisis baseline. VIX finished the cash session at 16.46, up 4.71%, still low in absolute terms. Delayed cross-asset context collected before this hour showed index futures marginally higher and Treasury futures marginally lower; it is used only as supporting confirmation and is superseded here by the fresher live quote showing NQ modestly lower and underperforming the broader index futures, which is consistent with a technology-specific catalyst.

The next scheduled catalysts are August PPI, core PPI and initial jobless claims at 12:30 UTC, with consensus near +0.4% month-on-month headline against +0.0% in July and core near +0.3%, followed by August existing home sales at 14:00 UTC, August CPI on 11 September, and the two-day FOMC meeting on 15-16 September with a Summary of Economic Projections. Those are checkpoints rather than observed structure: before a print, event importance and forecast dispersion inform Stress and Confidence, not Tail. Confidence of 88% reflects verified current futures, after-hours single-stock, volatility, yield, crude, geopolitical and calendar evidence for this hour.

lookbackSummary: Twenty-three of the preceding 24 clock-hours carry a published Claude assessment; the 10:00-11:00 UTC slot on 9 September has none and is marked unavailable. Tail ran between 7% and 9% through the Asian and European overnight, peaked at 20% in the 12:00 UTC hour, the single yellow WATCH slot in the window, then decayed through the US cash session and held at 8-9% from 21:00 UTC onward as price discovery stayed orderly. Stress climbed from 74% to an 83% peak and settled near 80-81%, driven by rates and crude rather than index path damage. Confidence held in an 87-89% band throughout.
outlookSummary: The forecast holds Tail in a 9-11% band through the Asian and European overnight, where the dominant mechanisms are absorption of the Nvidia antitrust report and headline discontinuity from the Strait of Hormuz into thin liquidity, rather than trend persistence. Tail then steps up into the 12:30 UTC PPI window and peaks at 20%, mapping to WATCH, in the 13:00 UTC hour where post-release repricing overlaps the US cash open. It decays back toward the overnight baseline through the US afternoon, with a small lift into the power hour before the 20:00 UTC close and a flat overnight path into Friday's CPI print. Stress stays extreme throughout, peaking at 87% in the event and cash-open hour, and Confidence declines from 88% to 77% as each slot moves further from verified live evidence.
